deviations.text: Seal was persisted before any new source or network read, but AGENTS.md and the relay and funnel method documents were first read after the seal (head and section skim only for the two methods). The seal field readsBeforeSeal says AGENTS-free.

While enumerating mirrors the worker ran git status in every source mirror (not only the named ones) and git cat-file on two; read-only commands that can refresh a git index stat cache. No file content, ref or object was changed by intent; mirror 7129340ae was not used as evidence.
A guessed path packages/parsers/src/ff-binaries.ts returned zero bytes (the real file is ffBinaries.ts); the failed read stays in the source path ledger.
Chrome for Testing latest-patch JSON exceeded the 2 MiB response cap; the capped 2097152 bytes were read and counted, the document was not parsed, and browser size stays UNKNOWN.

A first marker evaluator treated the PEP 440 wildcard in python_full_version markers as plain equality and dropped huggingface-hub from the closure, and a first wheel-tag filter rejected py3-none-win_amd64; both were fixed before any number was recorded, and only the corrected run feeds the evidence.
A full Apache licence text from PyPI JSON was printed to the console by mistake (output noise only; it is not stored in any output).
git ls-remote head observations are counted as two requests each (conservative accounting); one HTTPS list per repository was actually issued.

BtbN FFmpeg builds metadata was not read: the repository is named on ffmpeg.org's page, not by selected dependency metadata, so it was treated as outside the named read scope and left for Local admission.

The first SP-10 implementation searched for bare pattern names and matched the sealed prose that describes SP-10 itself (three hits inside planSeal, none a secret value). The sealed expectation (no secret or signed-URL value in any output) is unchanged; the detector was refined to value-shaped patterns and re-run. This is an implementation refinement recorded here, not a change of the seal.
